Camera mouse needs the camera.\n\nThe rear camera watches the surface under the phone and turns what it sees into pointer movement, the same way the sensor in an optical mouse does.
Camera access was refused. Grant it in Android Settings → Apps → WiFi Mouse → Permissions, or use trackpad mode instead.

The buttons at the top are the only part of the screen that responds to touch, so you can rest your hand anywhere below them. Double-tap that area to bring these controls back.

Hold the phone like a mouse, screen up, and slide it over a surface with some visible pattern: wood grain, fabric, paper with writing on it. Bare white desks and glass have nothing to track.

The tracking bar shows how well it can see. If it stays low:

• Turn the light on, for a dim surface
• Tilt the phone so the camera sits a little above the surface — phone cameras cannot focus on something pressed right against them
• Tap Refocus
• Try a surface with more pattern

It also works pointed at the room, held in the air like a laser pointer.

A phone camera manages about 30 readings a second where a real mouse manages thousands, so this always feels heavier than the trackpad. Use trackpad mode for precise work.
